summary: Receives and logs MIDI messages from a selected MIDI device into table rows with message type, channel, index, value, optional bytes, filters, and callbacks.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Enable input from the selected MIDI device

key_params.name: device
key_params.note: Path to the MIDI device Table DAT

key_params.name: id
key_params.note: MIDI device ID table path used by the device mapper workflow

key_params.name: value14
key_params.note: Combine paired MIDI controller messages into 14-bit values

key_params.name: skipsense
key_params.note: Do not log MIDI active sensing messages

key_params.name: skiptiming
key_params.note: Do not report MIDI timing messages

key_params.name: filter
key_params.note: Enable MIDI message filter parameters

key_params.name: message
key_params.note: Filter by MIDI message content

key_params.name: channel
key_params.note: Filter by MIDI channel in the 1-16 range

key_params.name: index
key_params.note: Filter by MIDI message index in the 1-128 range

key_params.name: value

key_params.name: callbacks

key_params.name: executeloc

common_gotchas: Device setup usually depends on the MIDI Device Mapper before the DAT receives messages.
Controller indices are documented as 1-based values from 1 to 128.
14-bit mode only outputs when matching MSB and LSB controller pairs are received.
High-rate MIDI streams can overflow small FIFO settings or call callbacks very frequently.
Use MIDI In DAT rather than MIDI In CHOP when message order, sysex, program changes, or note-on/note-off pairing is the data model.
Callback DATs must match the documented MIDI callback signature; mismatched arguments can make incoming events appear to vanish.
There is no MIDI Out DAT; scripted or channel-driven MIDI output goes through MIDI Out CHOP and its Python methods.
key_concepts: Receives MIDI messages from a selected MIDI input device into a DAT table.
Device and ID parameters choose the source device and connection id.
Value 14-bit output combines MIDI value bytes for higher-resolution controller data.
Message, channel, index, and value filters constrain captured MIDI traffic.
